statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let C be the set of valid cells. There exists a sequence ((i_k,j_k))_{k=0}^{len(r)-1} of cells in C such that: (1) every cell of C occurs exactly once in the sequence; (2) for every k with 0 <= k < len(r), r[k] = nums[i_k][j_k]; and (3) for all k,l with 0 <= k < l < len(r), either i_k+j_k < i_l+j_l, or i_k+j_k = i_l+j_l and i_k > i_l. Equivalently, r lists all entries nums[i][j] in increasing order of i+j, breaking ties by decreasing i.
preconditions: Let R = len(nums). The input satisfies: 1 <= R <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < R, 1 <= len(nums[i]) <= 100000; sum_{i=0}^{R-1} len(nums[i]) <= 100000; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < R and 0 <= j < len(nums[i]), 1 <= nums[i][j] <= 100000. A valid cell is a pair (i,j) with 0 <= i < R and 0 <= j < len(nums[i]).
